summary: Preserved candidate PR 2245's bounded LRU and paired ZMQ socket cleanup, reproduced review PR 2328's RLIMIT_NOFILE=128 failure against exact candidate commit 368fafdf463b9f208433d3254d7f3e1b42180a74, and corrected the unset cache default to derive a conservative cap from current descriptor headroom.

tests.what_was_measured: A fresh subprocess set its own soft RLIMIT_NOFILE to 128, left SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_ZMQ_SOCKET_CACHE_SIZE unset, and exercised real CommonKVManager._connect; candidate monitor socket creation raised zmq.error.ZMQError: Too many open files.

8 tests passed, including the same RLIMIT_NOFILE=128 subprocess completing 1,000 unique real PyZMQ endpoints with a derived/cache occupancy of 21 and 76 final open FDs, plus deterministic low/high limit boundary cases.
379 tests and 47 subtests passed across the registered disaggregation and environment suites.
All repository checks passed after ruff-format's one mechanical test-file reformat was applied.

remaining_limitations: The reporter's 16x NVIDIA H800 full-model and multi-node serving workload and weights were unavailable; the actual host-side CommonKVManager/PyZMQ path was reproduced instead.
The assigned single gfx950 GPU was not executed because no GPU kernel participates in this descriptor lifecycle.
No native source changed and repository-environment.json reports native as null, so no native rebuild was applicable.
The derived default is sampled at manager initialization; an explicitly oversized SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_ZMQ_SOCKET_CACHE_SIZE remains an operator override and can exceed the FD budget.
